findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "count_by_area" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_list" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_datasets, get_dataset, request_list, email_quote, get_quote, create_checkout, create_query_checkout, query_locations · Private data: search_datasets, get_dataset, count_locations, get_sample, get_quote, check_order, create_query_checkout, query_locations, buy_dataset · Public sink: relate_locations, cotenancy, request_list, send_feedback, email_quote, get_quote, query_locations.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_datasets, get_dataset, request_list, email_quote, get_quote, create_checkout, create_query_checkout, query_locations · Private data: search_datasets, get_dataset, count_locations, get_sample, get_quote, check_order, create_query_checkout, query_locations, buy_dataset · Public sink: relate_locations, cotenancy, request_list, send_feedback, email_quote, get_quote, query_locations

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
